CausalChain: Hypoxia in HCC -> HIF activation -> Upregulation of serine synthesis pathway (PHGDH, PSPH, SHMT2, etc.) -> Increased one‐carbon metabolism and S-adenosylmethionine production -> Epigenetic alterations (DNA and histone methylation) -> Silencing of immune-activating/drug-sensitizing genes -> Enhanced resistance to TKIs and ICIs
Hypothesis: In hypoxic HCC, HIF-mediated activation of the serine synthesis pathway increases one-carbon metabolism and SAM production, leading to epigenetic modifications that repress genes critical for drug sensitivity. Targeting this metabolic-epigenetic axis could reverse the transcriptional repression and restore sensitivity to TKIs and ICIs in resistant HCC.
Abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) displays significant resistance to both tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) and immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) largely due to the hypoxic tumor microenvironment which triggers a reprogramming of cellular metabolism. In hypoxic conditions, increased hypoxia‐inducible factor (HIF) activity upregulates pathways such as glycolysis, lactate and adenosinergic metabolism, mitochondrial suppression, and notably the serine synthesis pathway (SSP). We propose that the HIF‐driven boost in SSP not only reroutes glucose‐derived substrates to meet redox and energetic needs but also enhances one‐carbon metabolism. This leads to increased production of S‐adenosylmethionine (SAM), a key methyl donor, thereby inducing altered epigenetic landscapes. This epigenetic reprogramming may silence genes that promote sensitivity to conventional therapies, contributing to drug resistance in hypoxic HCC. Our work suggests that interrupting the HIF–SSP–one‐carbon–epigenetic axis may restore sensitivity to TKIs and ICIs.
